questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A plant flowers only once in 12 years. During its mass flowering, large tracts of the hills of Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu turn into blue stretches. The plant is:
questions.explanation:
Strobilanthus kunthiana (neelakuranji) flowers once in 12 years, and its flowering turns the hilly areas of these southern states blue.
Bamboo is the most tempting wrong option. It also flowers only once in its life, but generally after 50-100 years, and it is not linked to these blue hills.
Agave and Bryophyllum are known in this chapter for their vegetative propagules (bulbils and leaf buds), not for this flowering pattern.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In simple plants such as algae, bryophytes and pteridophytes, what is the medium through which male gametes are transferred to the female gamete?
questions.explanation:
In these simple plants the male gametes are motile and must swim to reach the egg.
NCERT states that water is the medium for gamete transfer in algae, bryophytes and pteridophytes.
A pollen tube is found only in seed plants. Air and insects carry pollen, not swimming gametes.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following plants is dioecious?
questions.explanation:
A dioecious plant bears male and female reproductive structures on separate plants.
Papaya has separate male and female plants, so it is dioecious. Date palm is another example.
Coconut and cucurbits bear staminate and pistillate flowers on the same plant, so they are monoecious.
Chara carries its male and female sex organs on the same plant, so it is also monoecious.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Drones in a honeybee colony develop from unfertilised eggs and are haploid.
(ii) The queen and worker bees develop from fertilised eggs and are diploid.
(iii) Drones form their gametes by meiosis.
(iv) In parthenogenesis, the female gamete develops into a new organism without fertilisation.
(v) In a diploid organism, syngamy produces a haploid zygote.
(vi) Parthenogenesis has been reported in some birds, such as the turkey.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: drones arise parthenogenetically from unfertilised eggs, so they are haploid.
(ii) Correct: the queen and workers come from fertilised eggs, so they are diploid.
(iii) Incorrect: drones are already haploid, so they form gametes by mitosis.
(iv) Correct: this is the definition of parthenogenesis.
(v) Incorrect: syngamy fuses two haploid gametes, giving a diploid zygote.
(vi) Correct: NCERT cites the turkey as an example.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about fertilisation is INCORRECT?
options: Bryophytes need water to transfer their male gametes, yet their fertilisation is internal
In angiosperms, the egg is formed inside the female body, where it fuses with the male gamete
Male gametes far outnumber female gametes in many plants, which compensates for the loss of male gametes during transfer
If water is needed as a medium for gamete transfer, fertilisation must be external
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct. In bryophytes and pteridophytes, male gametes swim through water to the egg, but the egg stays inside the female sex organ, so fertilisation is internal.
(2) Correct. This is how internal fertilisation works in angiosperms.
(3) Correct. Male gametes are produced in thousands of times greater numbers because many are lost on the way.
(4) Incorrect. Using water for transfer does not make fertilisation external, as bryophytes show.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are vegetative propagules of plants?
Runner, Zoospore, Tuber, Bulb, Gamete, Offset, Conidium, Sucker
questions.explanation:
Runner, tuber, bulb, offset and sucker are vegetative propagules. That makes 5.
Zoospores and conidia are asexual spores, not vegetative units of the plant body.
A gamete is a sexual reproductive cell.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Organism)
(a) Chlamydomonas
(b) Penicillium
(c) Hydra
(d) Sponge
List-II (Asexual structure)
(i) Conidia
(ii) Gemmules
(iii) Zoospores
(iv) Buds
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
(a) Chlamydomonas, an alga, produces motile zoospores, so a-iii.
(b) Penicillium, a fungus, produces conidia, so b-i.
(c) Hydra reproduces asexually by buds, so c-iv.
(d) Sponges form gemmules, so d-ii.
The tempting option (3) swaps buds and gemmules between Hydra and sponge.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about gamete formation and gamete transfer is incorrect?
options: Haploid organisms such as monerans, fungi, algae and bryophytes produce gametes by mitotic division
In bryophytes and pteridophytes the male gametes are non-motile, so water is not required for fertilisation
In diploid organisms, specialised cells called meiocytes undergo meiosis to form haploid gametes
In seed plants the non-motile male gametes are carried to the female gamete by pollen tubes
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: when the parent body is haploid, gametes are formed by mitosis.
(2) Incorrect: in many algae, bryophytes and pteridophytes the male gametes are motile. They need water to swim to the female gamete, and they are produced in very large numbers.
(3) Correct: meiocytes (gamete mother cells) undergo meiosis, so each gamete gets one set of chromosomes.
(4) Correct: in seed plants pollen grains carry the male gametes, and a pollen tube delivers them to the egg.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following mammals show an oestrus cycle?
Cow, sheep, rat, deer, dog, tiger, monkey, ape, human
questions.explanation:
Non-primate placental mammals show the oestrus cycle. These are the cow, sheep, rat, deer, dog and tiger, which makes 6.
Primates show the menstrual cycle instead. These are the monkey, ape and human, which makes 3.
So 6 of the nine mammals show the oestrus cycle.
The option '3' is a trap: it counts the menstrual-cycle animals instead.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Organisms showing external fertilisation release a large number of gametes into the surrounding water. The main purpose of this is to:
options: make sure every gamete develops into an adult
allow fertilisation without the other sex being present
questions.explanation:
Gametes released into water are scattered and diluted, so many of them never meet.
Releasing gametes in large numbers, in synchrony between the sexes, increases the chances of syngamy.
Option (1) is wrong because most offspring are lost, for example to predators.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Fungi and filamentous algae can multiply by fragmentation, each fragment growing into a new individual.
Statement II: Regrowth of a lost tail by a lizard is a form of reproduction because it increases the number of individuals.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. In fungi and filamentous algae, the body breaks into fragments, and each fragment grows into a new organism. This is asexual reproduction.
Statement II is incorrect. A lizard regrowing its tail only replaces a lost part. No new individual is formed, so the number of individuals stays the same. This is regeneration, not reproduction.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Ophioglossum has the highest chromosome number listed in the NCERT table, with 1260 chromosomes in its meiocytes. The chromosome number in its gametes is:
questions.explanation:
Ophioglossum, a fern, has 2n = 1260 in its meiocytes.
Meiosis halves the chromosome number, so each gamete has n = 1260 ÷ 2 = 630.
The value 2520 is a doubling, not a halving. The value 315 is a halving done twice.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In Bryophyllum, new plantlets develop from adventitious buds that arise at the:
options: Notches along the margin of the leaf
questions.explanation:
In Bryophyllum, adventitious buds form in the notches along the leaf margin. These are its vegetative propagules (leaf buds).
Nodes of an underground rhizome describes ginger, not Bryophyllum.
Root tips and floral bracts are not where its propagules form.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Life span is the period from birth to the natural death of an organism.
(ii) Larger organisms always have a longer life span than smaller organisms.
(iii) Crows and parrots are not very different in size, yet their life spans differ widely.
(iv) Single-celled organisms such as Amoeba and bacteria show no natural death.
(v) The mode of reproduction an organism adopts depends only on its habitat.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: NCERT defines life span as the period from birth to natural death.
(ii) Incorrect: life span is not correlated with size. A dog lives about 20 years, while a parrot lives about 140 years.
(iii) Correct: a crow lives about 15 years and a parrot about 140 years, though their sizes are similar.
(iv) Correct: the parent cell divides, and its body is distributed among the daughter cells, so there is no natural death.
(v) Incorrect: the mode of reproduction depends on habitat, internal physiology and genetic makeup together.
So three statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The vegetative propagule of Agave is the:
questions.explanation:
NCERT shows the bulbil as the vegetative propagule of Agave.
Offsets are seen in water hyacinth.
Eyes belong to the potato tuber.
Runners are creeping stems found in plants such as grasses, not in Agave.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A unisexual flower of a cucurbit plant that bears only stamens is termed:
questions.explanation:
A unisexual flower bearing only stamens is the male flower. It is called staminate.
A flower bearing only pistils is the female, or pistillate, flower.
A bisexual flower has both stamens and pistil.
A neuter flower has neither, so it does not fit a flower that has stamens.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In flowering plants, the period of growth from birth until the plant becomes capable of reproduction is called the
questions.explanation:
All organisms must grow and mature before they can reproduce.
The period from birth to reproductive maturity is called the juvenile phase. In plants it is called the vegetative phase.
The reproductive phase begins only after this phase ends, and in higher plants it is marked by flowering.
The senescent phase is old age, which comes after the reproductive phase.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a vegetative propagule of a flowering plant?
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists runner, rhizome, sucker, tuber, offset and bulb as vegetative propagules. These are units of the plant body that can form a new plant.
A conidium is an asexual spore produced by fungi such as Penicillium.
It is not a vegetative unit of a flowering plant.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Coconut is described as a monoecious plant even though its flowers are unisexual.
Reason (R): A monoecious plant bears both staminate and pistillate flowers on the same individual.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Each coconut flower is either staminate or pistillate, yet NCERT calls the coconut plant monoecious.
R is true. 'Monoecious' describes the whole plant: male and female flowers occur on the same individual.
R therefore explains why a plant with unisexual flowers can still be monoecious.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to the approximate life spans shown in NCERT, which of the following organisms can live for about 140 years?
questions.explanation:
NCERT's approximate life spans are: parrot about 140 years, dog about 20 years, crow about 15 years and rose 5-7 years.
Only the parrot reaches about 140 years.
The crow is a tempting choice because it is a bird of similar size, but it lives only about 15 years.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about vegetative propagation in plants is incorrect?
options: Plants raised from vegetative propagules are clones of the parent plant
Water hyacinth spreading over a pond can drain oxygen from the water and cause death of fishes
Vegetative propagules arise only from underground parts of the plant, such as tubers and rhizomes
Vegetative propagation is a form of asexual reproduction because no gametes are involved
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: there is a single parent and no gamete fusion, so the offspring are clones.
(2) Correct: NCERT notes that water hyacinth drains oxygen from water, leading to death of fishes.
(3) Incorrect: propagules also arise from aerial parts. Examples are leaf buds of Bryophyllum, bulbils of Agave and offsets of water hyacinth.
(4) Correct: vegetative propagation is asexual reproduction in plants.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A diagram shows a small outgrowth arising from the body wall of Hydra. The outgrowth enlarges, develops tentacles and finally detaches from the parent to live independently. This mode of asexual reproduction is
questions.explanation:
An outgrowth that develops on the parent and then separates as a new individual is called a bud. This mode of reproduction is budding.
NCERT cites buds in Hydra as an asexual reproductive structure.
Binary fission divides the whole parent into two equal halves, so it does not fit.
Regeneration only replaces a lost part, so it does not fit either.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (organism) with List-II (approximate life span) according to NCERT.
List-I:
(a) Butterfly
(b) Rice plant
(c) Crow
(d) Parrot
List-II:
(i) 15 years
(ii) 140 years
(iii) 1-2 weeks
(iv) 3-4 months
questions.explanation:
NCERT gives approximate life spans for several organisms.
(a) Butterfly lives only about 1-2 weeks, so it matches (iii).
(b) Rice plant completes its life in about 3-4 months, so it matches (iv).
(c) Crow lives about 15 years, so it matches (i).
(d) Parrot lives about 140 years, so it matches (ii).
The tempting option (3) swaps crow and parrot, even though these birds are similar in size.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A farmer raises an orchard of date palm entirely from seedlings and wants a good yield of dates. Which statement correctly applies to this crop?
options: Every date palm tree will bear fruits because each tree has both staminate and pistillate flowers
Only trees bearing pistillate flowers can form fruits, and their flowers must receive pollen from a different tree
Fruits can form by self-pollination within a single flower, since date palm flowers are bisexual
Trees bearing staminate flowers alone will produce most of the fruits
questions.explanation:
Date palm is dioecious. Each tree bears either only staminate flowers or only pistillate flowers.
Fruit develops from the ovary, which is present only in pistillate flowers. So only female trees can fruit.
Pollen has to come from a separate male tree, so self-pollination is impossible.
Option 1 describes a monoecious plant such as coconut. Option 3 wrongly calls the flowers bisexual. Male trees have no ovary, so option 4 fails.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following events in a flowering plant in the correct order:
(i) Pollen tube enters the ovule and discharges male gametes near the egg
(ii) Pollen grains germinate on the stigma
(iii) Pollen grains are transferred from anther to stigma
(iv) Syngamy forms a diploid zygote
(v) Pollen grains are formed in the anther
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Pollen grains carrying male gametes first form in the anther (v).
Step 2: Pollination transfers them to the stigma (iii).
Step 3: The pollen germinates on the stigma (ii) and a pollen tube grows into the ovule.
Step 4: The tube discharges the non-motile male gametes near the egg (i).
Step 5: Syngamy then produces the diploid zygote (iv).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The aquatic plant popularly called the 'terror of Bengal' is:
questions.explanation:
Water hyacinth (Eichhornia) is called the 'terror of Bengal'.
It spreads very fast by vegetative propagation (offsets) and chokes water bodies.
Bryophyllum and Agave are land plants, so the nickname does not fit them.
Ginger is a land plant that propagates by rhizome.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Organisms showing external fertilisation, such as bony fishes and frogs, release a very large number of gametes into the surrounding water.
Reason (R): Offspring formed by external fertilisation are extremely vulnerable to predators throughout their development up to adulthood.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. In external fertilisation the two sexes show great synchrony and shed huge numbers of gametes into water.
R is true. NCERT states that the major disadvantage of external fertilisation is that the offspring are highly vulnerable to predators until adulthood.
R does not explain A. Large numbers of gametes are released to raise the chances of syngamy in the open medium. Predation on offspring happens after fertilisation and is not the reason for gamete number.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following organisms is the main body haploid, so that its gametes are formed directly by mitotic division without any meiocyte?
questions.explanation:
NCERT: in many monerans, fungi, algae and bryophytes the plant body is haploid (n). Such a body can form haploid gametes by simple mitosis.
A moss is a bryophyte, so its haploid body forms gametes by mitosis.
Fern (a pteridophyte), mango (an angiosperm) and pine (a gymnosperm) have a diploid main plant body. In these plants, meiocytes undergo meiosis to reduce the chromosome number.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Coconut is monoecious and bears both staminate and pistillate flowers on the same plant
Papaya and date palm are dioecious, so male and female flowers occur on separate plants
Earthworm, sponge, tapeworm and leech are bisexual (hermaphrodite) animals
Cucurbits are called monoecious because each of their flowers is bisexual
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: coconut carries unisexual male and female flowers on the same plant, so it is monoecious.
(2) Correct: papaya and date palm are dioecious.
(3) Correct: NCERT lists these animals as bisexual. The cockroach, by contrast, is unisexual.
(4) Incorrect: cucurbits have unisexual flowers. They are monoecious because the staminate and pistillate flowers are borne on the same plant, not because each flower is bisexual.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In Agave, new plants are commonly produced from which vegetative propagules?
questions.explanation:
NCERT shows bulbils of Agave as vegetative propagules.
Bulbils are small fleshy buds formed on the plant. They drop off and grow into new plants.
Offsets are seen in water hyacinth and eyes in potato, so those options do not fit Agave.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following organisms produce gametes containing more than 15 chromosomes?
Human, House fly, Rat, Dog, Cat, Fruit fly, Apple, Maize
questions.explanation:
Halve each meiocyte number to get the gamete number.
Human 46 → 23 (yes). House fly 12 → 6 (no). Rat 42 → 21 (yes). Dog 78 → 39 (yes).
Cat 38 → 19 (yes). Fruit fly 8 → 4 (no). Apple 34 → 17 (yes). Maize 20 → 10 (no).
That gives five organisms.
Answer: (3)

questions.question:
Match List-I (plant) with List-II (vegetative propagule):
List-I: (A) Potato (B) Ginger (C) Agave (D) Water hyacinth
List-II: (i) Offset (ii) Bulbil (iii) Rhizome (iv) Eye
questions.explanation:
(A) Potato: tuber bearing eyes, so iv.
(B) Ginger: rhizome, so iii.
(C) Agave: bulbils, so ii.
(D) Water hyacinth: offsets, so i.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements about reproduction is incorrect?
options: Reproduction is a process by which an organism gives rise to young ones similar to itself
The way an organism reproduces depends on its habitat, internal physiology and other factors
The mode of reproduction is decided only by the body size of the organism
Reproduction may involve one parent or two parents
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: this is NCERT's definition of reproduction.
(2) Correct: habitat, internal physiology and several other factors, including genetic makeup, together decide how an organism reproduces.
(3) Incorrect: body size alone does not determine the mode of reproduction.
(4) Correct: asexual reproduction is uniparental, while sexual reproduction usually involves two parents.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Using the chromosome numbers of meiocytes given in NCERT, which of the following statements is correct?
options: A gamete of dog carries more chromosomes than a meiocyte of rat
A meiocyte of rice and a gamete of potato carry the same number of chromosomes
A zygote of maize formed by fusion of two gametes carries 40 chromosomes
A gamete of onion carries the same number of chromosomes as a meiocyte of house fly
questions.explanation:
(1) Incorrect: a dog gamete has 78/2 = 39 chromosomes, which is fewer than the 42 in a rat meiocyte.
(2) Correct: a rice meiocyte has 24 chromosomes, and a potato gamete has 48/2 = 24.
(3) Incorrect: each maize gamete has 10, so the zygote has 10 + 10 = 20, not 40.
(4) Incorrect: an onion gamete has 32/2 = 16, while a house fly meiocyte has 12.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (structure in a flower) with List-II (what it becomes after fertilisation).
List-I:
(A) Ovary
(B) Ovule
(C) Zygote
(D) Petals
List-II:
(i) Embryo
(ii) Wither and fall off
(iii) Fruit
(iv) Seed
questions.explanation:
Ovary becomes the fruit, which develops a protective pericarp: A-iii.
Ovule becomes the seed: B-iv.
Zygote develops into the embryo, which lies inside the seed: C-i.
Petals, like sepals and stamens, wither and fall off: D-ii.
A common error is swapping ovary with ovule, or zygote with ovule.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A filamentous green alga has a haplontic life cycle. Each vegetative cell of its filament has 16 chromosomes. Two of its gametes fuse to form a thick-walled zygote. After a period of rest, the zygote germinates and gives rise to new filaments. What are the chromosome numbers in the zygote and in the cells of the new filament, respectively?
questions.explanation:
Given: the haploid vegetative cells have n = 16, and the gametes are also haploid (16).
Fusion of two gametes gives a diploid zygote: 2n = 32.
In a haplontic cycle, the zygote divides by meiosis to form haploid spores with 16 chromosomes each.
These spores grow by mitosis into new filaments, so each cell has 16 chromosomes.
Choosing 32 for the filament wrongly assumes the zygote divides by mitosis.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following organisms are the two fusing gametes so similar in appearance that they cannot be categorised as male and female?
questions.explanation:
NCERT: in some algae the two gametes look alike and cannot be sorted into male and female. Such gametes are called homogametes or isogametes, and Cladophora is the standard example.
Fucus produces heterogametes (distinct male and female gametes), as shown in the NCERT figure.
Chara and Marchantia also form distinct antherozoids and eggs.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about asexual reproduction in unicellular organisms is INCORRECT?
options: In protists and monerans, cell division itself is a mode of reproduction
Amoeba and Paramecium reproduce by binary fission
In binary fission, each of the two halves rapidly grows into an adult
In yeast, budding involves equal division of the parent cell
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: in unicellular organisms, division of the parent cell gives rise to new individuals.
(2) Correct: both Amoeba and Paramecium divide by binary fission.
(3) Correct: after binary fission, each half rapidly grows into an adult.
(4) Incorrect: division in yeast is unequal and forms small buds.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Water hyacinth, introduced into India for its flowers, became one of the most invasive weeds and is called the 'terror of Bengal'.
Reason (R): Water hyacinth propagates vegetatively at a phenomenal rate and spreads over a water body in a short time.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Water hyacinth was brought to India for its beautiful flowers and leaf shape. It is now a notorious weed called the 'terror of Bengal'.
R is true. It propagates vegetatively, by offsets, very quickly. It covers ponds, drains oxygen from the water and kills fish.
This rapid vegetative spread is exactly why the weed is so hard to eradicate, so R explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following show internal fertilisation?
Fungi, reptiles, bryophytes, gymnosperms, a majority of algae, bony fishes, frogs, mammals
questions.explanation:
Internal fertilisation occurs in:
- fungi
- reptiles
- bryophytes
- gymnosperms
- mammals
That makes 5.
External fertilisation (in water) occurs in a majority of algae, bony fishes and frogs.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which feature distinguishes asexual reproduction in yeast from binary fission in Amoeba?
options: The division is unequal, and small outgrowths stay attached to the parent cell at first before separating and maturing
The parent cell divides into two equal daughter cells
The parent cell secretes a three-layered cyst before dividing
Motile asexual spores are released into water
questions.explanation:
In yeast, the division is unequal. Small buds form and initially remain attached to the parent cell. They later separate and mature into new yeast cells. This is budding.
Equal division into two daughter cells is binary fission, as seen in Amoeba and Paramecium.
Forming a three-layered cyst is encystation in Amoeba.
Motile spores, called zoospores, are formed by algae such as Chlamydomonas.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
i. Oestrus and menstrual cycles are cyclical changes in the ovaries, accessory ducts and hormones seen in females of placental mammals.
ii. Tigers and deer show menstrual cycles.
iii. A continuous breeder remains reproductively active throughout its reproductive phase.
iv. In perennial plants, the juvenile, reproductive and senescent phases are sharply demarcated.
v. In both plants and animals, hormones are responsible for the transitions between the juvenile, reproductive and senescent phases.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: Females of placental mammals show these cyclical reproductive changes.
(ii) Incorrect: Tigers and deer are non-primates, so they show the oestrus cycle, not the menstrual cycle.
(iii) Correct: Continuous breeders are active throughout the reproductive phase. Seasonal breeders are active only in favourable seasons.
(iv) Incorrect: In perennial plants these phases are difficult to define clearly.
(v) Correct: Hormones control the transitions between phases, and they interact with environmental factors.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the major disadvantage of external fertilisation, as seen in frogs and bony fishes?
options: The offspring are extremely vulnerable to predators
Male gametes cannot move in water
Meiosis does not occur before gamete formation
questions.explanation:
In external fertilisation, eggs and the young develop in open water without protection from the parent.
So the offspring are extremely vulnerable to predators, which threatens their survival up to adulthood.
Option (1) is wrong because these organisms release very large numbers of gametes.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Offspring produced by budding in yeast are genetically similar to the parent cell.
Reason (R): In yeast, the buds separate from the parent cell immediately after they are formed.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Budding is asexual and involves only one parent, so the offspring are clones of the parent.
R is false. The buds remain attached to the parent cell at first and separate only later before maturing.
Since R is false, it cannot explain A.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following mammals show an oestrus cycle?
Cow, rat, monkey, deer, human, tiger, ape, dog
questions.explanation:
The oestrus cycle is found in non-primate mammals. The menstrual cycle is found in primates.
Oestrus cycle: cow, rat, deer, tiger and dog. These are 5 non-primates.
Menstrual cycle: monkey, human and ape. These are primates.
So 5 of the listed mammals show an oestrus cycle.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the regulation of life phases and reproduction is incorrect?
options: In both plants and animals, hormones are responsible for the transitions between the juvenile, reproductive and senescent phases
Interaction between hormones and certain environmental factors regulates reproductive processes and the associated behaviour
In animals, the juvenile phase is followed by morphological and physiological changes before active reproductive behaviour begins
Hormones control phase transitions only in animals, while in plants these transitions depend solely on environmental factors
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: NCERT states that hormones drive the transitions between the three phases in both plants and animals.
(2) Correct: hormones interact with environmental factors to regulate reproductive processes and the behaviour linked to them.
(3) Correct: in animals, morphological and physiological changes come before active reproductive behaviour.
(4) Incorrect: hormones control phase transitions in plants as well, not only in animals.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following pairs do both organisms show syngamy in the external medium (water)?
questions.explanation:
In most aquatic organisms, such as most algae, fishes and amphibians, gametes fuse outside the body in water. This is external fertilisation.
Frogs (amphibians) and bony fishes show it, so option (1) fits.
Lizards and pigeons are reptiles and birds, which show internal fertilisation.
Mosses and ferns (bryophytes and pteridophytes) form the egg inside the female sex organ, where fertilisation takes place. The same is true of gymnosperms and angiosperms such as pine and mango.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In seed plants, the transfer of male gametes to the female gamete does not depend on water.
Reason (R): The male gametes of seed plants are flagellated and swim through the pollen tube to reach the egg.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. In seed plants, pollen grains carry the male gametes, and pollination brings them to the stigma, so no water medium is needed.
R is false. The male gametes of seed plants are non-motile.
The pollen grain germinates on the stigma. The pollen tube then grows and carries the non-motile male gametes to the ovule, close to the egg.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Cladophora
(B) Marchantia
(C) Coconut
(D) Leech
List-II
(I) Hermaphrodite animal
(II) Homogametes
(III) Monoecious plant with unisexual flowers
(IV) Heterothallic (dioecious) plant
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation:
A-II: Cladophora produces similar-looking gametes, which are homogametes.
B-IV: Marchantia has separate male and female thalli, so it is heterothallic (dioecious).
C-III: Coconut bears staminate and pistillate flowers on the same plant, so it is monoecious.
D-I: Leech has both sex organs in one body, so it is a hermaphrodite.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Although the potato tuber grows underground, it is regarded as a modified stem and not a root.
Reason (R): The potato tuber bears eyes, which are nodes carrying buds that can give rise to new shoots.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: the potato tuber is a swollen underground stem.
R is true: its eyes are nodes bearing axillary buds. Each eye can sprout into a new plant.
Nodes and buds are features of stems, not roots. So R correctly explains why the tuber is treated as a stem.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Water hyacinth, called the 'terror of Bengal', spreads very rapidly over standing water bodies mainly by means of:
questions.explanation:
Water hyacinth propagates vegetatively through offsets. This lets it spread fast over water and drain oxygen from the water body, which can kill fish.
Bulbils are the propagules of Agave.
Rhizomes are the propagules of ginger.
Leaf buds (adventitious buds on leaf margins) are the propagules of Bryophyllum.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Many mammals living in natural, wild conditions are called seasonal breeders.
Reason (R): Such mammals show reproductive cycles only during favourable seasons in their reproductive phase.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT states that many mammals, especially those living in the wild, are seasonal breeders.
R is true: these mammals show oestrus or menstrual cycles only during favourable seasons of their reproductive phase.
R explains A: they are called seasonal breeders precisely because their cycles are restricted to favourable seasons.
Mammals that stay reproductively active throughout the reproductive phase are called continuous breeders.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Plants raised from the eyes of a single potato tuber are clones of the parent plant.
Reason (R): Vegetative propagation involves only one parent and no fusion of gametes.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: offspring from potato eyes are morphologically and genetically similar to the parent, so they are clones.
R is true: vegetative propagules come from a single parent without gametic fusion. This is why the process counts as asexual reproduction.
The parent's genetic material simply passes unchanged through cell division, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following events:
(i) Formation of zoospores in Chlamydomonas
(ii) Formation of conidia in Penicillium
(iii) Regrowth of a lost tail in a lizard
(iv) Formation of gemmules in a sponge
(v) A Spirogyra filament breaking into pieces, each growing into a new filament
(vi) Formation of a bud in Hydra
(vii) Healing of a cut in human skin
How many of these are methods of asexual reproduction?
questions.explanation:
Reproduction must produce new individuals.
(i), (ii), (iv) and (vi) are asexual structures: zoospores, conidia, gemmules and buds. Each gives rise to new offspring.
(v) Fragmentation produces new filaments, so it is also asexual reproduction.
(iii) Lizard tail regrowth only replaces a lost part. The number of individuals stays the same, so this is regeneration, not reproduction.
(vii) Healing of a cut is tissue repair, not reproduction.
Total = 5.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Birds living in nature lay eggs only seasonally, but birds in poultry farms can be made to lay eggs throughout the year.
Statement II: Year-round egg laying in poultry farms is a reproductive adaptation of the birds to captivity.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT notes that wild birds lay eggs seasonally, while birds in captivity can be made to lay eggs all year.
Statement II is incorrect. In poultry farms, egg laying is not related to reproduction.
It is commercial exploitation for human welfare, not an adaptation of the birds.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(i) Every individual multicellular organism eventually undergoes natural death.
(ii) When an Amoeba undergoes binary fission, the parent ceases to exist as an individual without leaving a dead body.
(iii) Since Amoeba shows no natural death, a single Amoeba individual remains unchanged forever.
(iv) Reproduction is essential for the survival of an individual organism.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: NCERT states that death of every individual is certain, except in single-celled organisms.
(ii) Correct: the parent's body is shared between the daughter cells, so no corpse remains.
(iii) Incorrect: the parent Amoeba does not persist unchanged. It is replaced by two new daughter individuals.
(iv) Incorrect: reproduction is essential for continuity of the species, not for the survival of the individual.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
List-I gives organisms with the chromosome number of their meiocytes. Match each with the chromosome number of its gametes in List-II.
List-I:
A. Maize (20)
B. Apple (34)
C. Onion (32)
D. Dog (78)
List-II:
(i) 17
(ii) 39
(iii) 10
(iv) 16
questions.explanation:
Meiocytes (gamete mother cells) are diploid. Meiosis halves the chromosome number, so gametes are haploid.
Maize: 20 → 10, so A-(iii).
Apple: 34 → 17, so B-(i).
Onion: 32 → 16, so C-(iv).
Dog: 78 → 39, so D-(ii).
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (asexual reproductive structure) with List-II (organism in which it is seen).
List-I
A. Zoospore
B. Conidium
C. Bud
D. Gemmule
List-II
(i) Hydra
(ii) Chlamydomonas
(iii) Sponge
(iv) Penicillium
questions.explanation:
A. Zoospores are motile asexual spores of Chlamydomonas: (ii).
B. Conidia are asexual spores of the fungus Penicillium: (iv).
C. Buds are outgrowths that form new individuals in Hydra: (i).
D. Gemmules are internal asexual buds of sponges: (iii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In rotifers, honeybees and some lizards, the female gamete can develop into a new organism without fertilisation.
Reason (R): Syngamy is an obligatory event in all sexually reproducing organisms, without which a new individual cannot develop.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Development of a female gamete into a new organism without fertilisation is called parthenogenesis. NCERT cites rotifers, honeybees, some lizards and birds such as turkey.
R is false. Parthenogenesis itself shows that syngamy is not obligatory in every case. R in fact contradicts A.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In algae, bryophytes and pteridophytes, male gametes are produced in far larger numbers than female gametes. What is the main reason?
options: Male gametes are formed by meiosis, while female gametes are formed by mitosis
Many male gametes are lost while they travel through water to the female gamete
Several male gametes must fuse with one egg to form a zygote
Female gametes in these groups are motile and difficult to catch
questions.explanation:
In these groups the male gametes are motile and swim through water to reach the stationary female gamete.
During this transfer, a large number of male gametes fail to reach the egg and are lost.
Producing them in thousands makes up for this loss.
Option (3) is wrong because syngamy involves one male and one female gamete.
Option (4) is wrong because the female gamete is usually non-motile.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): There is no natural death in single-celled organisms such as Amoeba and bacteria.
Reason (R): During binary fission, the entire parental body is shared between the two daughter cells, so no dead parental body is left behind.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT notes that every individual eventually dies, except single-celled organisms, which show no natural death.
R is true. In binary fission the parent cell itself divides into two daughters, so its body is distributed between them.
Because no parent remains to die, R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following mammals shows a menstrual cycle during its reproductive phase?
questions.explanation:
Female placental mammals show cyclical changes in the ovaries, accessory ducts and hormones during the reproductive phase.
In primates (monkeys, apes and humans), this cycle is the menstrual cycle.
In non-primate mammals such as cows, dogs and tigers, it is the oestrus cycle.
So only the monkey, a primate, has a menstrual cycle.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the green alga Cladophora, the two fusing gametes look so alike that they cannot be classified as male or female. Such gametes are called:
questions.explanation:
NCERT: in a few algae the fusing gametes look so alike that they cannot be called male or female. These are homogametes, also called isogametes, and Cladophora is the standard example.
Heterogametes are dissimilar gametes, such as sperm and egg.
Antherozoids are male heterogametes, and zoospores are asexual spores, not gametes.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following organisms produce gametes that contain an ODD number of chromosomes?
Human, Rat, Rice, Apple, Onion, Cat, Maize
questions.explanation:
Halve each meiocyte (2n) number to get the gamete (n) number:
Human 46 → 23 (odd); Rat 42 → 21 (odd); Rice 24 → 12 (even); Apple 34 → 17 (odd); Onion 32 → 16 (even); Cat 38 → 19 (odd); Maize 20 → 10 (even).
The odd values belong to human, rat, apple and cat, which makes 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: A plant can be monoecious even if none of its flowers is bisexual
In heterogametic organisms, the male gamete is called an antherozoid or sperm and the female gamete an egg or ovum
A cucurbit plant cannot carry out pollination within the same flower, but pollen can still be transferred between flowers of the same plant
A plant such as papaya, which bears staminate and pistillate flowers on separate individuals, is described as homothallic
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct. Cucurbits and coconut have only unisexual flowers, yet both sexes occur on one plant, so they are monoecious.
(2) Correct. These are the NCERT names for heterogametes.
(3) Correct. A unisexual cucurbit flower cannot pollinate itself, but staminate and pistillate flowers occur on the same plant.
(4) Incorrect. Papaya has separate sexes, so it is heterothallic (dioecious), not homothallic.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The gametes of a diploid plant species X carry exactly as many chromosomes as the meiocytes of rice. Using the NCERT chromosome table, species X is:
questions.explanation:
Rice meiocytes have 24 chromosomes, so the gametes of X have n = 24.
The meiocytes of X therefore have 2n = 48.
In the table, 48 belongs to potato.
The other options do not fit: onion has 32, apple has 34 and maize has 20.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of meiocyte chromosome number and gamete chromosome number is correctly matched?
questions.explanation:
Meiocytes are diploid and divide by meiosis, so each gamete gets half the meiocyte's chromosome number.
Potato: 48 should give 24, not 12. Wrong.
Ophioglossum: 1260 gives 630. Correct.
Apple: 34 should give 17. Wrong.
Onion: 32 should give 16. The number can never double in a gamete. Wrong.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Zoospores can actively disperse in an aquatic medium, whereas conidia cannot.
Reason (R): Zoospores bear flagella, while conidia are non-motile.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Zoospores swim in water, which is why they are typical of algae and aquatic fungi. Conidia are passively dispersed.
R is true. Zoospores are flagellated and motile, while conidia, as in Penicillium, are non-motile.
The presence of flagella is exactly what allows zoospores to move actively. So R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
The chromosome number in the meiocyte (2n) is given for some organisms. How many of these pairs are correct?
(i) Rat – 42
(ii) Dog – 76
(iii) Onion – 32
(iv) Maize – 24
(v) Ophioglossum – 1260
(vi) House fly – 12
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: rat 2n = 42.
(ii) Incorrect: dog 2n = 78, not 76.
(iii) Correct: onion 2n = 32.
(iv) Incorrect: maize 2n = 20; 24 is the number for rice.
(v) Correct: Ophioglossum 2n = 1260.
(vi) Correct: house fly 2n = 12.
Four pairs are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Reproduction is regarded as a vital biological process mainly because it
options: is essential for the survival of every individual organism
ensures the continuity of the species, generation after generation
always produces offspring genetically identical to the parent
prevents the death of individual organisms
questions.explanation:
Reproduction is the process by which an organism gives rise to young ones similar to itself.
Its key role is to keep the species going, generation after generation, even though individuals die.
Option (1) is wrong because an individual can survive without reproducing. Reproduction matters for the species, not for the individual.
Option (3) is wrong because offspring of sexual reproduction are not identical to the parent.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following asexual reproductive structures is usually microscopic, flagellated and capable of swimming in water?
questions.explanation:
Zoospores are the most common asexual structures in algae and some fungi. They are usually microscopic, bear flagella and can move in water.
Conidia are also microscopic spores, but they are non-motile. This makes conidia the most tempting wrong option.
Gemmules and buds are multicellular structures. Neither of them swims.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following animals shows a menstrual cycle rather than an oestrus cycle?
questions.explanation:
Females of placental mammals show cyclical changes in the ovaries, the accessory ducts and their hormones.
In primates (monkeys, apes and humans), this cycle is called the menstrual cycle.
Non-primate mammals such as cows, sheep, rats, deer, dogs and tigers show the oestrus cycle instead.
So the monkey is the only primate among the options.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (organism) with List-II (chromosome number in its gamete):
List-I
(A) House fly
(B) Dog
(C) Butterfly
(D) Potato
List-II
(i) 39
(ii) 24
(iii) 6
(iv) 190
questions.explanation:
Each gamete number is half of the meiocyte (2n) number in the NCERT table.
(A) House fly: 12 → 6, so (iii).
(B) Dog: 78 → 39, so (i).
(C) Butterfly: 380 → 190, so (iv).
(D) Potato: 48 → 24, so (ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I:
(A) Cucurbits
(B) Papaya
(C) Leech
(D) Cockroach
List-II:
(I) Male and female individuals are separate animals
(II) Male and female flowers on the same plant
(III) Male and female flowers on different plants
(IV) Both male and female reproductive organs in the same animal
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
(A) Cucurbits are monoecious: male and female flowers on the same plant, so A-II.
(B) Papaya is dioecious: male and female flowers on separate plants, so B-III.
(C) Leech is hermaphrodite: both sexes in one individual, so C-IV.
(D) Cockroach is unisexual: separate male and female animals, so D-I.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The gametes of a liverwort are haploid even though they are produced by mitosis.
Reason (R): In liverworts the parent plant body that produces the gametes is itself haploid.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. All gametes are haploid, and a liverwort forms its gametes by mitosis.
R is true. Liverworts are bryophytes, whose main plant body is haploid.
Mitosis keeps the chromosome number unchanged. A haploid parent therefore directly gives haploid gametes, with no need for meiosis.
So R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Under unfavourable conditions, Amoeba withdraws its pseudopodia and secretes a three-layered hard covering around itself. This process is called:
questions.explanation:
When conditions are unfavourable, Amoeba withdraws its pseudopodia.
It then secretes a three-layered hard covering called a cyst. This process is called encystation.
Sporulation happens later, when the encysted Amoeba divides into many spores.
Budding and binary fission do not involve forming a protective cyst.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: A plant bearing both staminate and pistillate flowers on the same individual is called dioecious
Each flower of papaya bears both stamens and pistils
Most sexually reproducing organisms form morphologically distinct gametes, whereas the gametes of Cladophora cannot be categorised into male and female
In fungi, the term homothallic denotes the unisexual condition
questions.explanation:
(1) Incorrect. Male and female flowers on the same plant make it monoecious, not dioecious.
(2) Incorrect. Papaya is dioecious, so its flowers are unisexual.
(3) Correct. Most organisms produce heterogametes (antherozoid/sperm and egg/ovum), while Cladophora produces isogametes.
(4) Incorrect. Homothallic denotes the bisexual condition; heterothallic denotes the unisexual condition.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (organism) with List-II (asexual reproductive structure).
List-I:
A. Penicillium
B. Hydra
C. Sponge
D. Chlamydomonas
List-II:
(i) Zoospores
(ii) Gemmules
(iii) Conidia
(iv) Buds
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
A. Penicillium produces conidia, which are asexual spores: (iii).
B. Hydra reproduces asexually by budding: (iv).
C. Sponges form gemmules: (ii).
D. Chlamydomonas forms motile, flagellated zoospores: (i).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A female wild mammal shows cyclical changes in its ovaries and hormones, but these cycles occur only during a particular favourable season each year. During these cycles, the endometrium is not shed as menstrual bleeding. The animal is most likely
options: a primate and a continuous breeder
a non-primate and a seasonal breeder
a primate and a seasonal breeder
a non-primate and a continuous breeder
questions.explanation:
Step 1: there is cyclical ovarian and hormonal change but no menstrual bleeding. This means it has an oestrus cycle, so it is a non-primate (like deer or tiger).
Step 2: the cycles occur only in a favourable season, so it is a seasonal breeder.
Step 3: options with 'primate' fail because primates have menstrual cycles. 'Continuous breeder' fails because continuous breeders are active throughout the reproductive phase.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In viviparous animals, the young ones have a better chance of survival than in oviparous animals.
Reason (R): In viviparous animals, the zygote develops into a young one inside the body of the female, where it receives proper embryonic care and protection.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT notes that viviparous organisms, such as most mammals including humans, have better offspring survival.
R is true. The zygote develops into a young one inside the female's body.
R explains A. Development inside the mother gives proper embryonic care and protection.
Oviparous eggs, by contrast, are laid outside and face risks from the environment and predators.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (plant) with List-II (feature related to its vegetative propagation):
List-I
(A) Water hyacinth
(B) Bryophyllum
(C) Ginger
(D) Potato
List-II
(i) Buds arise from notches on leaf margins
(ii) Horizontal underground stem with nodes giving rise to new shoots
(iii) Swollen underground stem whose eyes bear buds
(iv) Aquatic weed spreading rapidly by offsets
questions.explanation:
(A) Water hyacinth is an aquatic weed that spreads by offsets, so A-(iv).
(B) Bryophyllum forms buds in the notches of its leaf margins, so B-(i).
(C) Ginger has a horizontal underground stem (rhizome) with nodes, so C-(ii).
(D) Potato has a swollen underground stem (tuber) with eyes, so D-(iii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Zoospores are usually microscopic, motile structures.
(ii) Conidia of Penicillium bear flagella.
(iii) Gemmules are asexual reproductive structures of sponges.
(iv) Buds of Hydra are formed by meiosis.
(v) Zoospores are sexual reproductive structures.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: NCERT describes zoospores as usually microscopic and motile.
(ii) Incorrect: conidia are non-motile and have no flagella.
(iii) Correct: sponges reproduce asexually by gemmules.
(iv) Incorrect: buds form by mitotic divisions, since asexual reproduction does not involve meiosis.
(v) Incorrect: zoospores are asexual structures.
Only 2 statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following organisms multiply asexually by the parent cell dividing into two halves (binary fission)?
Amoeba, Paramecium, bacteria, yeast, Penicillium, Hydra
questions.explanation:
Amoeba: yes, it divides by binary fission.
Paramecium: yes, it divides by binary fission.
Bacteria: yes, monerans divide into two.
Yeast: no, it reproduces by unequal division (budding).
Penicillium: no, it reproduces by conidia.
Hydra: no, it reproduces by buds.
Total = 3.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (asexual structure) with List-II (organism):
List-I
A. Zoospores
B. Conidia
C. Buds
D. Gemmules
List-II
(i) Penicillium
(ii) Sponge
(iii) Chlamydomonas
(iv) Hydra
questions.explanation:
A. Zoospores are the motile asexual structures of Chlamydomonas, so A matches (iii).
B. Conidia are the asexual spores of the fungus Penicillium, so B matches (i).
C. Buds are formed in Hydra, so C matches (iv).
D. Gemmules are formed in sponges, so D matches (ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Male gametes are produced in numbers several thousand times greater than female gametes. The main reason is that:
options: a large number of male gametes fail to reach the female gamete
each egg must fuse with many male gametes
male gametes are larger and need more nutrition
female gametes are motile and move away
questions.explanation:
During transfer, a large number of male gametes are lost and never reach the egg.
Producing them in huge numbers compensates for this loss.
Syngamy involves the fusion of only one male gamete with the egg.
In most organisms the female gamete is stationary and the male gamete is the smaller, motile one.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In Hydra, a bud develops as an outgrowth of the parent's body and can grow into a new individual.
Statement II: Gemmules of sponges are structures produced by sexual reproduction.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. In Hydra, a bud arises as an outgrowth of the body wall. It grows and develops into a new individual that is genetically like the parent.
Statement II is incorrect. NCERT lists gemmules of sponges along with zoospores, conidia and buds as asexual reproductive structures. Gemmules involve no gamete formation or fusion.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding reproductive cycles and breeding in animals is correct?
options: Menstrual cycle is seen in non-primate mammals such as cows, sheep and dogs
Oestrus cycle is the cyclical change seen in females of apes and humans
Birds living in nature lay eggs only seasonally, whereas poultry birds can be made to lay eggs throughout the year
Continuous breeders are reproductively active only during favourable seasons
questions.explanation:
(1) Incorrect: cows, sheep and dogs, being non-primates, show the oestrus cycle.
(2) Incorrect: apes and humans, being primates, show the menstrual cycle.
(3) Correct: wild birds breed seasonally, while poultry birds can be kept laying eggs all year round.
(4) Incorrect: activity only in favourable seasons describes seasonal breeders. Continuous breeders stay reproductively active throughout their reproductive phase.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The terms homothallic and heterothallic are used to describe the sexuality of fungi and plants.
Statement II: In a majority of sexually reproducing organisms, the fusing gametes are morphologically similar.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. In fungi and plants, homothallic or monoecious means the bisexual condition, and heterothallic or dioecious means the unisexual condition.
Statement II is incorrect. Most sexually reproducing organisms produce morphologically distinct heterogametes, the male sperm or antherozoid and the female egg or ovum. Similar homogametes occur only in a few algae such as Cladophora.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are cited in NCERT as organisms showing parthenogenesis?
Rotifers, honeybees, some lizards, turkey, earthworm, Hydra
questions.explanation:
Rotifers: yes, given as an example.
Honeybees: yes, drones develop from unfertilised eggs.
Some lizards: yes, given as an example.
Turkey: yes, given as an example.
Earthworm: no, it is a hermaphrodite that reproduces by cross-fertilisation.
Hydra: no, it is known for budding and is not an example of parthenogenesis.
So the total is 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In diploid organisms, the specialised cells that undergo meiosis to produce gametes are called:
questions.explanation:
In organisms with a diploid parental body, gametes form by meiosis in specialised cells. These are the meiocytes, also called gamete mother cells.
Zoospores, conidia and gemmules are asexual reproductive structures. They are not gamete-forming cells.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about post-fertilisation development:
(i) Embryogenesis involves both cell division and cell differentiation.
(ii) The cell divisions during embryogenesis are meiotic, so that the diploid number is maintained.
(iii) Cell differentiation helps groups of cells undergo modifications to form specialised tissues and organs.
(iv) In flowering plants, the zygote develops into the seed and the ovule develops into the embryo.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct. Embryogenesis, the development of an embryo from the zygote, needs both cell division and cell differentiation.
(ii) Incorrect. The divisions are mitotic. Meiosis would halve the chromosome number, not maintain it.
(iii) Correct. Differentiation forms specialised tissues and organs.
(iv) Incorrect. The roles are reversed: the zygote becomes the embryo and the ovule becomes the seed.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following animals are bisexual (hermaphrodite)?
Earthworm, Cockroach, Tapeworm, Leech, Sponge, Frog
questions.explanation:
Bisexual animals have both male and female reproductive organs in the same individual.
Earthworm, tapeworm, leech and sponge are bisexual, which makes 4.
Cockroach and frog are unisexual because their sexes are separate.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following groups does syngamy normally take place outside the body of the parents, in water?
questions.explanation:
Fertilisation that takes place in the external medium (water), outside the body, is called external fertilisation.
NCERT gives a majority of algae, fishes and amphibians as examples. Bony fishes release their gametes into water.
Reptiles, birds and mammals are terrestrial higher animals. They show internal fertilisation.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Strobilanthus kunthiana (neelakuranji) flowers only once in about 12 years.
Reason (R): Strobilanthus kunthiana is an annual plant that dies soon after flowering.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT notes that Strobilanthus kunthiana flowers once in 12 years. In September–October 2006 it turned large stretches of the hilly areas of Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu blue.
R is false. An annual completes its whole life cycle within one year, so it cannot wait 12 years to flower. This plant is a perennial with a long vegetative phase.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: After fertilisation in a flower, which part remains attached to the plant and develops further, while the other floral parts wither and fall off?
questions.explanation:
After fertilisation, the sepals, petals and stamens of most flowers wither and fall off.
The pistil stays attached to the plant.
Its ovary develops into the fruit, and its ovules develop into seeds.
Some plants keep their sepals (persistent calyx), but even there the sepals do not form the fruit. So the pistil is the part that develops further.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Bamboo species flower every year once they reach maturity, like mango and apple.
Statement II: Strobilanthus kunthiana (neelakuranji) flowers once in 12 years, turning large hilly tracts blue when it blooms.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. Bamboo species flower only once in their lifetime, generally after 50–100 years. They then produce a large number of fruits and die. Mango and apple, by contrast, flower seasonally every year.
Statement II is correct. Strobilanthus kunthiana flowers once in 12 years; it last flowered in 2006 in the hills of Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about vegetative propagules are correct?
(i) The 'eyes' of a potato tuber are nodes bearing buds.
(ii) Ginger propagates by its rhizome, which is a modified root.
(iii) In Bryophyllum, adventitious buds arise from notches present at the leaf margins.
(iv) Agave propagates by bulbils.
(v) Water hyacinth propagates by offsets.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: the eyes are nodes, and their buds give rise to new plants.
(ii) Incorrect: a rhizome is an underground modified stem, not a root.
(iii) Correct: buds develop from the notches along the leaf margin of Bryophyllum.
(iv) Correct: Agave bears bulbils.
(v) Correct: water hyacinth spreads by offsets.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In Marchantia, the gametes are produced by mitotic division.
Reason (R): The parental plant body in bryophytes is haploid.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
Marchantia is a liverwort, which is a bryophyte. Its gamete-producing plant body is haploid.
A haploid cell cannot halve its chromosome number by meiosis to form gametes, so gametes arise by mitosis. A is true.
R is true, and it directly explains why mitosis is used.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A unisexual flower that bears only pistils and no stamens is called a
questions.explanation:
In flowering plants, a unisexual female flower bears pistils and is called pistillate.
A unisexual male flower bears stamens and is called staminate.
'Monoecious' describes a whole plant that carries both male and female flowers. It does not describe a single flower.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) In Protists and Monerans, cell division is itself a mode of reproduction.
(ii) Asexual reproduction always involves the formation of gametes.
(iii) In budding of yeast, the parent cell divides into two equal halves.
(iv) Zoospores are microscopic, motile asexual reproductive structures.
(v) Asexual reproduction is common among organisms with a relatively simple organisation, such as fungi and algae.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct. In unicellular protists and monerans, the parent cell divides to form new individuals.
(ii) Incorrect. Asexual reproduction involves a single parent and may occur with or without gamete formation. It is typically without gametes.
(iii) Incorrect. Budding is unequal division that produces small buds.
(iv) Correct. Zoospores, such as those of Chlamydomonas, are motile.
(v) Correct. Asexual reproduction is common in simple organisms such as fungi and algae.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Oviparous animals such as reptiles and birds lay fertilised eggs in a safe place. These eggs are covered by:
options: A thin, soft gelatinous jelly only
questions.explanation:
Reptiles and birds are oviparous. They lay fertilised eggs covered by a hard calcareous (calcium-rich) shell in a safe place.
The young hatch after a period of incubation.
Gelatinous jelly surrounds the eggs of animals such as frogs, not those of reptiles and birds.
Cellulose is found in plant cell walls, and chitin forms the exoskeleton of arthropods.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Strobilanthus kunthiana (neelakuranji) is known for its unusual flowering. How often does it flower?
options: Twice a year, in every monsoon
questions.explanation:
NCERT gives Strobilanthus kunthiana as an example of unusual flowering behaviour.
It flowers once in 12 years. Its last recorded flowering was in September–October 2006.
Its mass flowering turned large hilly tracts of Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu into blue stretches.
'Once in 50–100 years' is the tempting wrong option, but that figure describes bamboo species.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The potato tuber is regarded as a modified stem because it bears nodes (eyes) that carry buds.
Statement II: The rhizome of ginger is a modified root that stores food.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The eyes of a potato are nodes bearing buds, and having nodes with buds is a feature of stems, not roots.
Statement II is incorrect. A ginger rhizome is an underground stem, not a root.
It also has nodes and internodes, and its buds give rise to new shoots.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
