Statement I: Crows and parrots are not very different in body size, yet their life spans differ widely.
Statement II: The life span of an organism is directly correlated with its body size.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. A crow lives about 15 years and a parrot about 140 years, although the two birds are of similar size.
Statement II is incorrect. NCERT stresses that life span is not necessarily correlated with size.
The crow-parrot example is the very evidence used to show this.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
A pond containing Amoeba dries up gradually and is later refilled with water. The following events occur in the Amoeba:
P. Encysted Amoeba divides by multiple fission
Q. Pseudopodia are withdrawn
R. Cyst wall bursts and pseudopodiospores are liberated
S. A three-layered hard covering is secreted around the cell
Which option gives the correct sequence of events?
questions.explanation:
When conditions become unfavourable as the pond dries, Amoeba first withdraws its pseudopodia (Q).
It then secretes a three-layered hard cyst around itself (S). This is encystation.
When favourable conditions return, the encysted Amoeba divides by multiple fission (P), producing many minute amoebae called pseudopodiospores.
Finally, the cyst wall bursts and the spores are released (R).
Option (2) is wrong because the pseudopodia must be withdrawn before the cyst forms.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Bamboo species
(B) Strobilanthus kunthiana
(C) Continuous breeder
(D) End of reproductive phase
List-II
(i) Flowers once in 12 years
(ii) Reproductively active throughout the reproductive phase
(iii) One of the parameters of senescence
(iv) Flowers once in a lifetime, generally after 50–100 years
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
A-(iv): bamboo species flower only once in their lifetime, generally after 50–100 years. They produce many fruits and then die.
B-(i): Strobilanthus kunthiana flowers once in 12 years.
C-(ii): continuous breeders stay reproductively active throughout their reproductive phase.
D-(iii): NCERT treats the end of the reproductive phase as one parameter of senescence (old age).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about post-fertilisation events are correct?
(i) Every sexually reproducing organism, including humans, begins life as a single-celled zygote.
(ii) In organisms with a haplontic life cycle, the zygote divides by mitosis to give rise to haploid individuals.
(iii) Embryogenesis involves both cell division and cell differentiation.
(iv) The chances of survival of the young are greater in oviparous animals than in viviparous animals.
(v) The pericarp of a fruit is protective in function.
(vi) In haplontic organisms, the cells of the adult body are diploid.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: the zygote is the starting point of every sexually reproducing organism.
(ii) Incorrect: in haplontic forms the zygote divides by meiosis. This forms haploid spores, which grow into haploid individuals.
(iii) Correct: cell division increases the number of cells, and differentiation forms specialised tissues and organs.
(iv) Incorrect: viviparous young survive better because of proper embryonic care and protection.
(v) Correct: the pericarp is protective.
(vi) Incorrect: in haplontic organisms the adult is haploid. Only the zygote is diploid.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Every plant that bears unisexual flowers must be dioecious.
Statement II: In Marchantia, gametes are formed by mitotic division because the gamete-producing thallus is itself haploid.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. Cucurbits and coconut bear unisexual (staminate and pistillate) flowers, yet both are monoecious because both kinds of flower occur on the same plant.
Statement II is correct. Gametes are always haploid. A haploid parent such as the Marchantia thallus therefore produces gametes by mitosis, while diploid parents use meiosis.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are post-fertilisation events in a flowering plant?
Embryogenesis
Gametogenesis in anthers
Development of the ovary into a fruit
Pollination
Maturation of ovules into seeds
Meiosis in meiocytes
questions.explanation:
Post-fertilisation events are those that occur after the zygote is formed.
Embryogenesis (zygote → embryo) is post-fertilisation.
Ovary developing into fruit is post-fertilisation.
Ovules maturing into seeds is post-fertilisation.
Gametogenesis, pollination (gamete transfer) and meiosis in meiocytes all happen before fertilisation.
Total = 3.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (organism) with List-II (asexual reproductive structure):
List-I
A. Chlamydomonas
B. Penicillium
C. Hydra
D. Sponge
List-II
(i) Gemmule
(ii) Bud
(iii) Conidium
(iv) Zoospore
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
A. Chlamydomonas produces motile zoospores, so A matches (iv).
B. Penicillium produces non-motile conidia, so B matches (iii).
C. Hydra forms buds, so C matches (ii).
D. Sponges form gemmules, so D matches (i).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The meiocytes of onion contain 32 chromosomes. How many chromosomes will be present in each of its gametes?
questions.explanation:
Meiocytes are diploid (2n). Here 2n = 32.
Meiosis places only one set of chromosomes in each gamete, so a gamete has n chromosomes.
n = 32 ÷ 2 = 16.
The value 32 would be wrong, because gametes do not keep the meiocyte number.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The aquatic weed called the 'terror of Bengal' spreads rapidly over water bodies mainly through which mode of reproduction?
questions.explanation:
The 'terror of Bengal' is water hyacinth (Eichhornia).
It propagates vegetatively through offsets at a phenomenal rate. It can cover a water body in a short time.
It is a flowering plant, but its rapid spread is due to vegetative propagation, not seeds. Spores and binary fission do not apply to it.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes asexual reproduction in yeast?
options: The cell divides into two equal halves that separate at once
The cell divides unequally to form small buds that stay attached to the parent at first and later separate
The cell secretes a cyst and divides into many spores
Two cells fuse and then divide by meiosis
questions.explanation:
In yeast, cell division is unequal and small buds are produced.
The buds remain attached to the parent cell at first. They later separate and mature into new yeast cells.
Equal division into two halves is binary fission, as seen in Amoeba and Paramecium.
Forming a cyst and dividing into many spores is multiple fission in Amoeba.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the two statements.
Statement I: The zygote is the vital link that ensures continuity of a species from one generation to the next.
Statement II: In birds, the fertilised egg is laid covered by a hard calcareous shell, and the embryo develops outside the mother's body.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Every sexually reproducing organism begins life as a single-celled zygote. The zygote therefore links one generation to the next.
Statement II is correct. Reptiles and birds are oviparous. They lay fertilised eggs covered by a hard calcareous shell in a safe place, and the young develop outside the mother's body. After incubation, the young hatch.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In seed plants, which structure acts as the carrier of the male gametes?
questions.explanation:
In seed plants the male gametes are non-motile and are carried inside pollen grains.
Pollen grains form in the anther and are transferred to the stigma during pollination.
The ovule contains the egg, not the male gametes. The anther wall only produces the pollen and does not travel with it.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the following statements:
(i) Annual and biennial plants show clear-cut vegetative, reproductive and senescent phases, whereas in perennials these phases are hard to define.
(ii) Mango, apple and jackfruit flower continuously throughout the year once they mature.
(iii) Cyclical changes in reproductive organs of females of cows, sheep, rats, deer, dogs and tiger are called the oestrus cycle, while in primates they are called the menstrual cycle.
(iv) Birds in nature lay eggs only seasonally, but in captivity (poultry farms) they can be made to lay eggs throughout the year.
(v) Continuous breeders are fertile only during favourable seasons.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: phases are distinct in annuals and biennials but unclear in perennials.
(ii) Incorrect: these perennials show seasonal flowering, not continuous flowering.
(iii) Correct: non-primate mammals show the oestrus cycle; primates (monkeys, apes, humans) show the menstrual cycle.
(iv) Correct: poultry birds can be made to lay eggs throughout the year.
(v) Incorrect: continuous breeders are reproductively active throughout their reproductive phase. Breeding only in favourable seasons describes seasonal breeders.
Correct = 3.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (organism) with List-II (asexual reproductive structure).
List-I:
(A) Chlamydomonas
(B) Penicillium
(C) Hydra
(D) Sponge
List-II:
(i) Bud
(ii) Gemmule
(iii) Zoospore
(iv) Conidium
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
(A) Chlamydomonas, a unicellular alga, forms motile zoospores, so A matches (iii).
(B) Penicillium, a fungus, produces non-motile conidia, so B matches (iv).
(C) Hydra produces buds as outgrowths of its body, so C matches (i).
(D) Sponges form gemmules, so D matches (ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: A gamete of rat contains 21 chromosomes
A human meiocyte has the same chromosome number as a human somatic cell
In a haploid parent, gametes formed by mitosis have half the chromosome number of the parent's vegetative cells
The zygote of maize contains 20 chromosomes
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: rat has 42 in its meiocytes, so each gamete has 21.
(2) Correct: meiocytes are diploid like somatic cells, so both have 46.
(3) Incorrect: mitosis keeps the chromosome number unchanged. Gametes of a haploid parent have the same number as its vegetative cells.
(4) Correct: two maize gametes (n = 10) fuse to give a zygote with 20.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I:
(A) Pollination
(B) Syngamy
(C) Parthenogenesis
(D) Pollen tube
List-II:
(i) Development of a female gamete into a new individual without fertilisation
(ii) Carries non-motile male gametes to the ovule
(iii) Transfer of pollen grains from anther to stigma
(iv) Fusion of male and female gametes
questions.explanation:
(A) Pollination is the transfer of pollen from anther to stigma, so A matches (iii).
(B) Syngamy is the fusion of gametes that forms the zygote, so B matches (iv).
(C) Parthenogenesis is development of a female gamete without fertilisation, so C matches (i).
(D) The pollen tube carries the male gametes to the ovule, so D matches (ii).
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
A student examines a flower of a pea plant about two weeks after fertilisation. The pod remains attached to the plant, while the other floral whorls have dropped off. How many of the following statements about this stage are correct?
(i) The zygote has developed into the embryo inside the seed.
(ii) The ovules have developed into seeds.
(iii) The wall of the pod (pericarp) has developed from the ovary wall.
(iv) The zygote first developed a thick wall and underwent a resting period before dividing.
(v) Sepals, petals and stamens generally wither and fall off after fertilisation.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: the zygote undergoes embryogenesis to form the embryo.
(ii) Correct: ovules mature into seeds.
(iii) Correct: the ovary becomes the fruit, and its wall forms the pericarp.
(iv) Incorrect: a thick-walled, resting zygote that resists desiccation is typical of many algae and fungi, not flowering plants.
(v) Correct: these whorls wither and fall, but the pistil stays attached.
That gives 4 correct statements.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The vegetative cell of a haploid unicellular alga similar to Chlamydomonas contains 12 chromosomes. It produces zoospores, and each zoospore grows into a new individual. The number of chromosomes in each zoospore will be
questions.explanation:
Zoospores are asexual reproductive structures.
Asexual reproduction does not involve meiosis, and the zoospores are formed by mitotic divisions.
Mitosis keeps the chromosome number unchanged, so each zoospore carries the same 12 chromosomes as the parent cell. The zoospore offspring are clones of the parent.
The value 6 would require meiosis, and 24 would require gametic fusion. Neither occurs during zoospore formation.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Zoospores, the most common asexual reproductive structures of many algae, are:
options: Microscopic, non-motile structures with a thick wall
Multicellular outgrowths of the parent body
Haploid gametes that fuse in water
questions.explanation:
Members of Kingdom Fungi and simple plants such as algae reproduce through special asexual structures.
The most common of these are zoospores, which are microscopic and motile. An example is Chlamydomonas.
They are not gametes, because they develop into new individuals without any fusion.
Non-motile asexual spores, such as conidia, are a different type of structure.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a flowering plant, where is the zygote formed after fertilisation?
options: In the wall of the ovary
questions.explanation:
In flowering plants the male gamete reaches the egg, which lies inside the ovule. Fertilisation, and so zygote formation, takes place there.
The ovule later becomes the seed that holds the embryo.
The ovary wall is a tempting choice, but it becomes the pericarp of the fruit. It does not hold the egg.
The anther makes pollen, and the stigma only receives pollen.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which asexual reproductive structure is produced by the fungus Penicillium?
questions.explanation:
NCERT names conidia as the common asexual reproductive structures of Penicillium.
Conidia are non-motile spores.
Zoospores are the most tempting wrong choice because they are also fungal and algal spores. However, they are motile and flagellated, as in Chlamydomonas and aquatic fungi, and they are not formed by Penicillium.
Gemmules occur in sponges, and buds occur in Hydra.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Annual and biennial plants show clear-cut vegetative, reproductive and senescent phases.
Statement II: In higher plants, the end of the vegetative phase is marked by flowering.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. According to NCERT, annual and biennial plants show clear-cut vegetative, reproductive and senescent phases. In perennial species these phases are very difficult to define clearly.
Statement II is correct. In higher plants, the onset of flowering marks the end of the vegetative phase and the start of the reproductive phase.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which pair of organisms provides the best evidence that life span is NOT correlated with body size?
questions.explanation:
Evidence against a size-life span link needs organisms of similar size with very different life spans.
Crow and parrot are similar in size, yet live about 15 years and about 140 years. This is the best evidence.
In each of the other pairs, the larger organism also lives longer:
- butterfly (1-2 weeks) vs crow (15 years)
- rice (3-4 months) vs rose (5-7 years)
- crow (15 years) vs dog (20 years)
These pairs fit a size trend, so they cannot disprove it.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following pairs correctly matches an organism with its mode of asexual reproduction?
questions.explanation:
Paramecium is a unicellular protist. The parent cell divides into two to form two new individuals, which is binary fission.
Yeast reproduces by budding, not multiple fission.
Amoeba reproduces by binary fission. When encysted, it reproduces by multiple fission. It does not bud.
Penicillium forms conidia. Zoospores are formed by algae such as Chlamydomonas.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the phases of life in plants is correct?
options: Perennial plants show clear-cut vegetative, reproductive and senescent phases
Annual and biennial plants show clear-cut vegetative, reproductive and senescent phases
The vegetative phase has the same length in all plants
The end of the vegetative phase cannot be recognised in any higher plant
questions.explanation:
(1) Incorrect: in perennial species, the three phases are very difficult to define clearly.
(2) Correct: annuals and biennials show distinct vegetative, reproductive and senescent phases.
(3) Incorrect: the length of the juvenile (vegetative) phase varies from organism to organism.
(4) Incorrect: in higher plants, the end of the vegetative phase is easily seen because the plant comes to flower.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Offspring formed by external fertilisation are extremely vulnerable to predators, which threatens their survival up to adulthood.
Statement II: In a majority of algae, fertilisation takes place inside the body of the organism.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Syngamy outside the body produces young that are exposed in the medium, usually water, and many are eaten by predators. This is one reason such organisms release huge numbers of gametes.
Statement II is incorrect. NCERT cites the majority of algae, along with bony fishes and amphibians, as examples of external fertilisation.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In many fungi and algae, the zygote develops a thick wall. What is the main role of this wall?
options: It helps the zygote move quickly to a new habitat
It lets the zygote photosynthesise efficiently
It protects the zygote from desiccation and damage while it rests before germinating
It allows the zygote to fuse with another gamete
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that in fungi and algae the zygote often forms a thick wall that resists desiccation (drying) and damage.
Such a zygote goes through a period of rest and germinates later, when conditions are favourable.
The wall is protective. It is not for movement or photosynthesis.
Once a zygote is formed, it does not fuse with another gamete.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In plants, the period of growth an organism must pass through before it can reproduce sexually is known as the:
questions.explanation:
Every organism must reach a certain stage of growth and maturity before it can reproduce sexually.
In animals this period is called the juvenile phase. In plants it is called the vegetative phase.
Senescence is the old-age phase that follows the reproductive phase, so it cannot come before reproduction.
Dormancy is a resting condition and is not a growth phase that leads to maturity.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Cyclical changes in the activities of the ovaries and accessory ducts, together with hormonal changes, occur during the reproductive phase of female placental mammals. In which one of the following animals is this cycle called a menstrual cycle rather than an oestrus cycle?
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that the menstrual cycle occurs only in primates, such as monkeys, apes and humans.
Non-primate mammals, such as cows, sheep, rats, deer, dogs and tigers, show an oestrus cycle instead.
The monkey is the only primate among the options.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The body cells of a honeybee queen contain 32 chromosomes. What is the chromosome number in the body cells of a worker bee and a drone, respectively?
questions.explanation:
The queen is diploid (2n = 32), so each egg she produces is haploid (n = 16).
Workers develop from fertilised eggs. An egg (16) fused with a sperm (16) gives a diploid worker with 32 chromosomes.
Drones develop from unfertilised eggs by parthenogenesis, so they are haploid with 16 chromosomes.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Fertilisation in bryophytes and pteridophytes depends on the availability of water.
Reason (R): Their male gametes are motile and require a medium to swim to the egg.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: bryophytes and pteridophytes need water (for example, a film of water) for fertilisation.
R is true: their male gametes are motile and swim to reach the stationary egg.
The need for a medium for the motile gametes is exactly why water is required, so R explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following birds is cited in NCERT as an example in which the female gamete can develop into a new organism without fertilisation?
questions.explanation:
Development of a female gamete into a new organism without fertilisation is called parthenogenesis.
NCERT lists rotifers, honeybees, some lizards and birds such as the turkey as examples.
Pigeon, sparrow and peacock are not given as examples.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Marchantia is a heterothallic (unisexual) organism.
Reason (R): In Marchantia, antheridiophores and archegoniophores are borne on separate male and female thalli.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT uses 'heterothallic' and 'dioecious' for the unisexual condition, and shows Marchantia as unisexual.
R is true. The male thallus bears antheridiophores and a separate female thallus bears archegoniophores.
Because the two sexes sit on different thalli, Marchantia is unisexual. So R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following features:
(i) Offspring are clones of the parent
(ii) Only a single parent is involved
(iii) Meiosis precedes formation of the offspring
(iv) The parent ceases to exist as a distinct individual after reproduction
(v) New plants arise from structures such as rhizome, runner or tuber
(vi) No gametes are formed or fused
How many of these features are common to BOTH binary fission in Amoeba and vegetative propagation in ginger?
questions.explanation:
(i) Common: both are asexual, so the offspring are morphologically and genetically similar to the parent (clones).
(ii) Common: both involve a single parent.
(iii) Neither: asexual reproduction involves only mitosis.
(iv) Binary fission only: the Amoeba parent divides into two daughters, whereas the ginger plant continues to live.
(v) Vegetative propagation only: these are multicellular propagules.
(vi) Common: gametes are not involved in either.
Common features = 3.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a haploid green alga, two gametes each carrying 10 chromosomes fuse to form a zygote. The zygote gives rise to spores that grow into new plants, and these plants later form gametes. What is the chromosome number in the spores and in the new gametes, respectively?
questions.explanation:
Given: each gamete has n = 10, so the zygote has 2n = 20.
In haploid organisms the zygote divides by meiosis to form haploid spores, so each spore has 10 chromosomes.
The spores grow into haploid plants (n = 10).
These plants form gametes by mitosis, so the gametes keep 10 chromosomes.
Option (2) wrongly assumes a second meiosis during gamete formation.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: An encysted Amoeba divides by multiple fission when favourable conditions return, producing many minute amoebae called pseudopodiospores.
Statement II: Inside the cyst, Amoeba divides by binary fission while conditions are still unfavourable, and only two daughter amoebae are released.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. When favourable conditions return, the encysted Amoeba divides by multiple fission. This produces many minute amoebae, called pseudopodiospores. The cyst wall then bursts and releases them.
Statement II is incorrect on two counts. The division is multiple fission, not binary fission, and it gives many offspring rather than two. It also happens when conditions become favourable, not during unfavourable conditions.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The vegetative cells of a filamentous green alga contain 12 chromosomes each. In its life cycle, meiosis takes place in the zygote. What is the chromosome number in its gametes, in its zygote and in the cells of the new filament formed after the zygote germinates, respectively?
questions.explanation:
Meiosis in the zygote means the adult filament is haploid, so n = 12.
A haploid body forms gametes by mitosis, so each gamete has 12 chromosomes.
Fusion of two gametes produces a diploid zygote with 24 chromosomes.
The zygote then divides by meiosis, giving haploid cells that grow into a new filament with 12 chromosomes per cell.
Option (4) is tempting but wrongly assumes the zygote divides by mitosis.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In frogs, both sexes show great synchrony in releasing their gametes.
Reason (R): The gametes are released into water, so they must be shed at the same time and place for syngamy to have a good chance of occurring.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT notes that organisms with external fertilisation, such as frogs and bony fishes, show great synchrony between the sexes.
R is true. Gametes released into water disperse, so they can meet only if both sexes release them together.
This need is exactly why synchrony exists, so R explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I:
(A) Frog
(B) Moss
(C) Pea
(D) Rabbit
List-II:
(i) Internal fertilisation; non-motile male gametes carried by pollen tube
(ii) External fertilisation in water
(iii) Internal fertilisation inside the body of a terrestrial higher animal
(iv) Internal fertilisation; motile male gametes need water to reach the egg
questions.explanation:
(A) Frog is an amphibian. Syngamy occurs in water, so A matches (ii).
(B) Moss is a bryophyte. Its swimming male gametes reach the egg inside the female sex organ, so B matches (iv).
(C) Pea is an angiosperm. A pollen tube carries its male gametes, so C matches (i).
(D) Rabbit is a mammal and shows internal fertilisation, so D matches (iii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements comparing zoospores and conidia is INCORRECT?
options: Zoospores bear flagella whereas conidia lack them
Both give rise to new individuals without fusion of gametes
Conidia swim actively in water while zoospores are passively dispersed by air
Offspring from both are genetically similar to the single parent
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: zoospores are flagellated, while conidia are non-motile.
(2) Correct: both are asexual structures, so no gametic fusion is involved.
(3) Incorrect: this reverses the facts. Zoospores are the swimming spores of algae and aquatic fungi, and conidia cannot swim.
(4) Correct: asexual offspring come from a single parent and are near-identical clones.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In many fungi and algae, the zygote formed after fertilisation develops a thick wall. What is the main function of this wall?
options: It helps the zygote attach to the substratum for photosynthesis
It resists desiccation and damage so the zygote can survive a period of rest before germination
It stores reserve food for immediate mitotic divisions
It prevents meiosis from occurring in the zygote
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that in fungi and algae the zygote develops a thick wall that resists desiccation and damage.
The protected zygote then rests for a period before it germinates. This helps it survive unfavourable conditions.
The wall does not stop meiosis. In haplontic forms the zygote itself undergoes meiosis on germination.
The wall is not concerned with attachment or photosynthesis.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
A student observes two unicellular organisms under a microscope.
Organism X: a small outgrowth appears on one side of the cell, stays attached to it for a while, and later detaches and grows into a new cell.
Organism Y: the cell lies inside a thick, three-layered wall and its nucleus divides repeatedly. Later the wall bursts and releases many tiny cells.
Identify the processes and the likely organisms.
options: X: binary fission in Paramecium; Y: budding in yeast
X: budding in yeast; Y: multiple fission in encysted Amoeba
X: zoospore formation in Chlamydomonas; Y: binary fission in Amoeba
X: budding in yeast; Y: conidia formation in Penicillium
questions.explanation:
X shows unequal division, with a bud that stays attached at first and separates later. This is budding, as in yeast.
Y shows a cell inside a three-layered cyst whose nucleus divides repeatedly, releasing many minute cells. This is multiple fission in encysted Amoeba.
Binary fission gives just two equal halves, so it does not fit either organism.
Conidia are spores formed by the fungus Penicillium, not division products released from a cyst.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following pairs of chromosome numbers, written as meiocyte : gamete.
(i) Human 46 : 23
(ii) Housefly 12 : 6
(iii) Rat 42 : 24
(iv) Potato 48 : 24
(v) Onion 32 : 8
How many of the above pairs are correct?
questions.explanation:
Meiosis halves the chromosome number, so a gamete has half the number found in the meiocyte.
(i) Correct: 46 → 23.
(ii) Correct: 12 → 6.
(iii) Incorrect: a rat meiocyte with 42 chromosomes gives gametes with 21, not 24.
(iv) Correct: 48 → 24.
(v) Incorrect: an onion meiocyte with 32 chromosomes gives gametes with 16, not 8.
Three pairs are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following plants bears male and female flowers on separate individuals?
questions.explanation:
A plant whose male and female flowers are borne on separate individuals is dioecious. NCERT gives papaya and date palm as examples.
Coconut is monoecious: male and female flowers occur on the same tree.
Cucumber and pumpkin are cucurbits, which NCERT cites as monoecious.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In organisms with internal fertilisation, very few eggs are produced, but the male gametes are produced in large numbers.
Statement II: In every organism with internal fertilisation, the male gamete is motile and moves on its own to reach the egg.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. With internal fertilisation, egg numbers are few while male gametes are numerous.
Statement II is incorrect because of the word 'every'. In seed plants the male gametes are non-motile, and pollen tubes carry them to the egg.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a honeybee colony, the queen is diploid with 32 chromosomes in her body cells. Drones (males) develop from unfertilised eggs by parthenogenesis. Workers develop from fertilised eggs. What are the chromosome numbers in a body cell of a drone, a sperm produced by that drone, and a body cell of a worker, respectively?
questions.explanation:
Drone: it grows from an egg that is not fertilised. The egg carries 32/2 = 16 chromosomes, so the drone is haploid with 16.
Sperm: the drone is already haploid, so it forms gametes by mitosis, not meiosis. Each sperm therefore keeps 16 chromosomes. Option (2) wrongly assumes a further halving to 8.
Worker: a 16-chromosome sperm fuses with a 16-chromosome egg, giving a diploid zygote with 32.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In many algae and fungi, the zygote develops a thick wall around itself.
Reason (R): The thick wall allows the zygote to undergo mitosis immediately after its formation.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. In many algae and fungi the zygote builds a thick wall.
R is false. The wall makes the zygote resistant to desiccation and damage, so it can pass through a period of rest before it germinates. It does not cause immediate division.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (part present in a flower at fertilisation) with List-II (its fate after fertilisation).
List-I:
(a) Ovary
(b) Ovules
(c) Zygote
(d) Stamens
List-II:
(i) Develops into the embryo
(ii) Wither and fall off
(iii) Develops into the fruit
(iv) Develop into seeds
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
(a) Ovary – (iii): the ovary develops into the fruit, whose thick protective wall is the pericarp.
(b) Ovules – (iv): the ovules mature into seeds.
(c) Zygote – (i): the zygote develops into the embryo, which lies inside the seed.
(d) Stamens – (ii): sepals, petals and stamens generally wither and fall off. Only the pistil remains attached.
Option (1) swaps the ovary and the ovules, which is the most common error.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following show the bisexual (homothallic / monoecious / hermaphrodite) condition?
Chara, Marchantia, earthworm, leech, cockroach, coconut, papaya, date palm
questions.explanation:
Bisexual: Chara (male and female sex organs on the same plant), earthworm and leech (hermaphrodites), and coconut (monoecious).
Unisexual: Marchantia (separate male and female thalli), cockroach (separate sexes), and papaya and date palm (dioecious).
This gives 4 bisexual organisms.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Gemmules, which are special asexual reproductive structures, are characteristic of
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists gemmules as the asexual reproductive structures of sponges.
The other organisms in the options use different structures:
Hydra reproduces by buds.
Penicillium reproduces by conidia.
Chlamydomonas reproduces by zoospores.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The offspring produced when an Amoeba divides by binary fission are referred to as a clone.
Reason (R): These offspring arise from a single parent without fusion of gametes and are morphologically and genetically similar to the parent and to one another.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Binary fission is asexual reproduction by a single parent.
R is true. No gametes fuse, so the parent's genetic material is copied and shared between the offspring. The offspring are therefore exact copies of the parent and of each other.
NCERT defines a clone as a group of morphologically and genetically similar individuals. R therefore correctly explains why the offspring are called a clone.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Water hyacinth, introduced into India for its attractive flowers, has become one of the most troublesome aquatic weeds and is called the 'terror of Bengal'.
Reason (R): Water hyacinth propagates vegetatively at a phenomenal rate and drains oxygen from the water body.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Water hyacinth was brought in for its beautiful flowers and leaf shape, and it now chokes water bodies.
R is true. It spreads very fast by vegetative propagation (offsets) and depletes oxygen in the water, which kills fishes.
This rapid spread and harm to the water body is exactly why it became a feared weed, so R explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
A. Bamboo
B. Strobilanthus kunthiana
C. Dog
D. Human
List-II
I. Menstrual cycle
II. Flowers once in 12 years
III. Oestrus cycle
IV. Flowers once in its lifetime, generally after 50–100 years
Choose the correct answer.
questions.explanation:
A-IV: Bamboo species flower only once in their lifetime, generally after 50–100 years. They produce a large number of fruits and then die.
B-II: Strobilanthus kunthiana (neelakuranji) flowers once in 12 years.
C-III: The dog is a non-primate mammal, so it shows the oestrus cycle.
D-I: Humans are primates, so they show the menstrual cycle.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The asexual spores of Chlamydomonas are able to swim in water because they are
options: non-motile conidia carried by water currents
gemmules enclosed in a protective coat
gametes that fuse to form a zygote
questions.explanation:
Chlamydomonas reproduces asexually by zoospores.
Zoospores are usually microscopic and motile, and they bear flagella that let them swim.
Conidia are non-motile, so option (1) fails.
Gemmules belong to sponges.
Gametes are involved in sexual reproduction, not asexual reproduction.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A student cuts a potato tuber into several pieces and plants them in moist soil. Pieces carrying at least one eye sprout into new plants, but pieces cut only from regions between the eyes fail to sprout. The best explanation is that:
options: Pieces without eyes lack stored food needed for growth
Eyes are nodes bearing buds with meristematic cells, while internodal tissue lacks such buds
Eyes contain gametes that fuse after planting to form new plants
Pieces without eyes are root tissue, which cannot form shoots
questions.explanation:
The eyes of a potato are nodes, and each carries an axillary bud.
Buds have meristematic cells that can divide to form new shoots and roots. That is why nodes give rise to vegetative propagules.
Internodal pieces also hold plenty of starch, but they have no buds, so they cannot sprout.
Gametes are not involved, and the tuber is stem tissue, not root.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Bamboo species flower only once in their lifetime, generally after 50–100 years, then produce a large number of fruits and die.
Statement II: Strobilanthus kunthiana flowers every year during September–October in the hilly areas of Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Bamboo flowers only once in its life, usually after 50–100 years, sets plenty of fruit and then dies.
Statement II is incorrect. Strobilanthus kunthiana (neelakuranji) flowers once in 12 years, not every year. Its last mass flowering in those hilly areas was in September–October 2006.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In Bryophyllum, new plantlets develop from:
options: Buds arising in the notches along the leaf margins
Bulbils formed in place of flowers
questions.explanation:
NCERT describes leaf buds of Bryophyllum. These are adventitious buds that arise from the notches at the leaf margins.
They grow into plantlets when they come in contact with moist soil.
Eyes belong to potato and rhizome nodes to ginger, so those options fail.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (organism) with List-II (approximate life span):
List-I: (A) Butterfly (B) Rice plant (C) Rose (D) Dog
List-II: (i) 5-7 years (ii) 1-2 weeks (iii) 20 years (iv) 3-4 months
questions.explanation:
(A) Butterfly lives 1-2 weeks, so A matches (ii).
(B) Rice plant lives 3-4 months, so B matches (iv).
(C) Rose lives 5-7 years, so C matches (i).
(D) Dog lives about 20 years, so D matches (iii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In NCERT, morphologically and genetically similar individuals produced by asexual reproduction from a single parent are called:
questions.explanation:
In asexual reproduction a single parent produces offspring without gamete fusion.
These offspring are identical to one another and are exact copies of the parent.
Such morphologically and genetically similar individuals are called clones.
Propagules are the units used in vegetative propagation. Gametes and zygotes belong to sexual reproduction.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The meiocyte of the fern Ophioglossum contains 1260 chromosomes. How many chromosomes will be present in each of its gametes?
questions.explanation:
A meiocyte is diploid (2n), and meiosis halves the chromosome number.
So each gamete has n = 1260 ÷ 2 = 630 chromosomes.
1260 is the meiocyte (2n) value, not the gamete value.
2520 would mean the number had doubled, and 315 would mean it had been halved twice.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In NCERT, the life span of an organism is defined as the period from
options: fertilisation to the onset of reproductive maturity
birth to the natural death of the organism
birth to the end of the reproductive phase
the juvenile phase to the senescent phase
questions.explanation:
NCERT defines life span as the period from birth to the natural death of an organism.
It covers the whole life of the individual, including the juvenile, reproductive and senescent phases.
Option (3) is tempting, but it ends at the close of the reproductive phase. An organism usually lives on after that, through senescence.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Based on the approximate life spans given in NCERT, how many of the following organisms have a life span exceeding 10 years?
Butterfly, rice plant, rose, crow, dog, parrot, tortoise
questions.explanation:
Butterfly (1-2 weeks): no.
Rice plant (3-4 months): no.
Rose (5-7 years): no.
Crow (15 years), dog (20 years), parrot (140 years) and tortoise (100-150 years): yes.
So 4 organisms exceed 10 years. Rose is the usual trap, since it is perennial but lives under 10 years.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In bryophytes and many algae, gametes are produced without meiosis.
Reason (R): In these organisms the parental plant body is haploid, so gametes are formed by mitotic division.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. In monera, fungi, algae and bryophytes, gamete formation does not involve meiosis.
R is true. In these groups the parental body is already haploid, so gametes are made by mitosis.
R correctly explains A: because the body is already haploid, a further reduction division is not needed to form gametes.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the phases of life are correct?
(i) In annual and biennial plants, the vegetative, reproductive and senescent phases are clearly identifiable.
(ii) In perennial plants, the three phases are as clearly demarcated as in annuals.
(iii) The juvenile phase in plants is known as the vegetative phase.
(iv) In animals, the end of the reproductive phase can be considered one of the parameters of senescence.
(v) Senescence is accompanied by changes in the body such as slowing of metabolism.
(vi) The juvenile phase is of the same duration in all organisms.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: annuals and biennials show the three phases clearly.
(ii) Incorrect: in perennials the phases are very difficult to define clearly.
(iii) Correct: in plants the juvenile phase is called the vegetative phase.
(iv) Correct: the end of the reproductive phase marks the onset of senescence (old age).
(v) Correct: senescence brings concomitant changes such as slowing of metabolism.
(vi) Incorrect: the juvenile phase varies in length from organism to organism.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following animals are oviparous?
Crocodile, Pigeon, Human, Turtle, Rabbit, Hen, Cat
questions.explanation:
Oviparous animals lay eggs with a calcareous shell, and the young develop outside the mother's body.
Crocodile and turtle are reptiles, so they are oviparous.
Pigeon and hen are birds, so they are oviparous.
Human, rabbit and cat are mammals, so they are viviparous.
That gives 4 oviparous animals.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are vegetative propagules in plants?
Runner, sucker, zoospore, bulbil, conidium, offset, rhizome, seed
questions.explanation:
Vegetative propagules (5): runner, sucker, bulbil, offset and rhizome. Each is a vegetative part that can give a new plant.
Zoospores and conidia are asexual spores of algae and fungi. They are not vegetative organs.
A seed is formed after fertilisation, so it is a product of sexual reproduction.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Drones of a honeybee colony produce their sperms by meiosis.
Statement II: Drones develop from unfertilised eggs.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement II is correct: drones arise from unfertilised eggs by parthenogenesis, so they are haploid.
Statement I is incorrect: a haploid body cannot undergo reduction division to form gametes.
Drones therefore produce sperms by mitosis.
The queen and the workers are diploid because they develop from fertilised eggs.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In seed plants, the male gametes are non-motile. How do they reach the female gamete?
options: By swimming through a film of water
By being carried in the pollen tube
By wind currents after the pollen grain bursts
By amoeboid movement through the stigma
questions.explanation:
Seed plants (gymnosperms and angiosperms) show internal fertilisation.
Their male gametes are non-motile. The pollen tube carries them to the egg inside the ovule.
Option (1) describes bryophytes and pteridophytes, which have motile male gametes that need water.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (organism) with List-II (chromosome number in its gametes):
List-I: (A) Rat (B) Dog (C) Cat (D) House fly
List-II: (i) 19 (ii) 6 (iii) 21 (iv) 39
questions.explanation:
Each gamete number is half the meiocyte number from the NCERT table.
Rat: 42 → 21, so A-(iii).
Dog: 78 → 39, so B-(iv).
Cat: 38 → 19, so C-(i).
House fly: 12 → 6, so D-(ii).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Parthenogenesis is the development of a new organism from a female gamete without fertilisation. Which of the following is NOT an example of parthenogenesis given in NCERT?
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists rotifers, honeybees, some lizards and birds such as the turkey as organisms that show parthenogenesis.
The earthworm is a bisexual (hermaphrodite) animal. It reproduces by cross-fertilisation, with gametes contributed by two individuals.
So the earthworm is not an example of parthenogenesis.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Species X is an aquatic animal. During one short breeding period it sheds thousands of eggs into a pond, where it is joined by males shedding sperm. Species Y is a land animal. It lays a few shelled eggs. Which inference is most consistent with NCERT's account of fertilisation?
options: X shows internal fertilisation and its young have higher survival than Y's
X shows external fertilisation and many of its young are lost to predators; Y shows internal fertilisation
Both show external fertilisation because both lay eggs
Y shows external fertilisation because it lays eggs outside its body
questions.explanation:
X is aquatic, releases huge numbers of gametes and sheds them in synchrony with males. All of these mark external fertilisation, in which the young are highly vulnerable to predators.
Y is terrestrial and produces few eggs. Its eggs are fertilised inside the female before being laid, so it shows internal fertilisation, as in reptiles and birds.
Options (3) and (4) are wrong because laying eggs outside the body is oviparity, which is not the same as external fertilisation.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following groups is the parental body haploid, so that gametes are produced by mitotic division?
questions.explanation:
NCERT: in several members of monera, fungi, algae and bryophytes, the parental body is haploid. These organisms form gametes by mitosis.
In pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms the parental body is diploid. Gametes are formed by meiosis in meiocytes.
So only bryophytes fit.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following animals has separate male and female individuals (unisexual)?
questions.explanation:
NCERT gives the cockroach as its example of a unisexual animal, with separate male and female individuals.
Earthworm, leech and tapeworm each carry both male and female reproductive organs in one body. They are bisexual animals, or hermaphrodites.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following organisms are bisexual, i.e. hermaphrodite animals or monoecious plants?
Earthworm, Leech, Sponge, Tapeworm, Cockroach, Marchantia, Chara, Date palm
questions.explanation:
Bisexual: earthworm, leech, sponge and tapeworm are hermaphrodite animals. Chara bears both male and female sex organs on the same plant.
Unisexual: cockroach has separate sexes. Marchantia has separate male and female thalli. Date palm is dioecious.
The total of bisexual organisms is 5.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In organisms with a haplontic life cycle, the zygote divides by meiosis to form haploid spores.
Statement II: The haploid spores formed from such a zygote grow into haploid individuals.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. In a haplontic life cycle the diploid zygote is the only diploid stage, and it undergoes meiosis (zygotic meiosis).
Statement II is correct. Meiosis produces haploid spores, which grow by mitosis into haploid individuals.
So the dominant, free-living phase of such organisms is haploid.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A farmer cuts a potato tuber into several pieces and plants them. Some pieces sprout into new plants, while others simply rot without sprouting. The most likely reason is that the pieces that failed:
options: Contained too little stored starch to support growth
Lacked an eye, i.e., a node bearing a bud capable of growth
Were planted upside down, so the roots grew upward
Lacked chlorophyll and so could not photosynthesise
questions.explanation:
The eyes of a potato tuber are nodes that bear buds.
The buds contain meristematic cells that can divide and form a new shoot.
A piece without an eye has only storage tissue, so it cannot form a new plant.
Stored starch alone cannot produce a shoot, and orientation does not matter.
The tuber is underground, so photosynthesis is not needed for sprouting.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about water hyacinth is INCORRECT?
options: It was introduced into India because of its beautiful flowers and the shape of its leaves
It grows in standing water and drains oxygen from it, which leads to the death of fishes
Its rapid spread over water bodies is mainly due to the large number of seeds it produces sexually
It is one of the most invasive weeds and can cover a water body in a short time
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: it was introduced into India for its flowers and leaf shape.
(2) Correct: it grows in standing water and drains its oxygen, killing fish.
(3) Incorrect: its spread is due to fast vegetative propagation by offsets, not seed production.
(4) Correct: it is a highly invasive weed that spreads quickly over water bodies.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology (pre-2023 edition), Ch 1 · Reproduction in Organisms
